pinned.digest_source: the digest GitHub records for the release asset (release API digest field), read 2026-11-18

method: wpr records the providers below, under the instance name, to a file inside the bundle for the window; PresentMon then reads that file with --etl_file and prints its CSV on stdout, captured under the artifact cap; the file is deleted after it was read because a WPR merged recording may carry the network adapter hardware and IP addresses. Live PresentMon is not run: in realtime mode it opens a PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION handle to every presenting process (OutputThread.cpp QueryProcessName, v2.6.0) and enables SeDebugPrivilege when it can (MainThread.cpp); with --etl_file both are skipped (the same two functions test args.mEtlFileName)

providers.source: EnableProvidersListing: ProcessStart_Start, ProcessStop_Stop, ProcessRundown_Info, plus EVENT_CONTROL_CODE_CAPTURE_STATE for the rundown of processes already running

EnableProvidersListing: the present history, flip, blit, queue packet, VSync, context, device, hardware queue and DMA packet events for track display and track GPU; the Performance keyword (0x4000000000000000) is removed as PresentMon does; capture state for Context_DCStart and Device_DCStart
EnableProvidersListing: TokenCompositionSurfaceObject_Info, TokenStateChanged_Info (track display), InputDeviceRead_Stop, RetrieveInputMessage_Info, OnInputXformUpdate_Info (track input)

EnableProvidersListing: GetPresentHistory_Info, SCHEDULE_PRESENT_Start, SCHEDULE_SURFACEUPDATE_Info, FlipChain_Pending, FlipChain_Complete, FlipChain_Dirty; Composition (0x1) is added for Windows 10, where PresentMon swaps it for Scheduling (0x80)

output_paths_recorded_as: bundle relative paths; the processes received the absolute paths of the same files in this bundle, in double quotes
recording_deleted_because: a WPR merged recording may hold the network adapter hardware and IP addresses (SystemConfig_NIC through the merge's NetworkInterface custom event); the project keeps those out of every bundle, so the recording is read on the PC and deleted. recording.json keeps its size, SHA-256 and header

disk_budget.note: the session stops at session_file_max_bytes (MaximumFileSize, sequential); the merged file is checked against merged_file_max_bytes and deleted either way; the CSV is captured under csv_max_bytes by the process runner, which stops PresentMon at the cap; the merge temp folder is removed on every path. The peak is bounded by the session file plus the merged file plus the CSV plus two console streams (peak_bytes_bound), and ETW keeps 200 MB free on the system drive

option_citations.--etl_file: Analyze an ETW trace log file instead of the actively running processes.
option_citations.--qpc_time: Output the CPU start time as a performance counter value.
option_citations.--process_name: Only record processes with the specified exe name. This argument can be repeated to capture multiple processes.
option_citations.wpr -start: Starts one or more profiles. -filemode: recording is done in file mode. -recordtempto: the temporary folder path that the recording is saved to.
option_citations.wpr -status: Displays the status of an active recording (if any). collectors: lists collector information, with Events Lost per collector and the enabled providers.
option_citations.wpr -stop: Cancels and saves the recording initiated by WPR (if any) to the given file. -skipPdbGen disables dynamic generation of pdbs for .NET modules.
option_citations.wpr -cancel: Cancels the current recording without saving the recorded data.
option_citations.-instancename: Specifies a name to uniquely identify the tracing instance. This option can be applied to any commands that manipulate the logging session. -instancename must be the last parameter.
